answers.ref_note: The reference is the clique tree (bn_exact.py).

notes.agrum: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

notes.agrum: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

answers.ref_note: The reference is the clique tree (bn_exact.py).

notes.agrum: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

notes.agrum: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

notes.agrum: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

answers.ref_note: The reference is the clique tree (bn_exact.py).

notes.agrum: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

notes.agrum: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

notes.agrum: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

notes.agrum: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

notes.agrum: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

notes.agrum: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

answers.ref_note: The reference is the clique tree (bn_exact.py).

notes.agrum: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

answers.ref_note: The reference is the clique tree (bn_exact.py).

notes.agrum: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

module AleaProgram
using Alea
# Julia would spend more time optimizing the long straight-line functions
# below than running them takes: they are interpreted, and Alea's own
# methods compile as usual.
Base.Experimental.@compiler_options compile=min optimize=0 infer=false

const EV = Ref{AnyBool}(true)
observe!(path, c) = (EV[] = EV[] & (!path | c); true)

function shr(x::DistUInt{W}, n::Integer) where W
    k = min(n, W)
    DistUInt{W}(vcat(fill(false, k), x.bits[1:W - k]))
end

components(x::Tuple) = reduce(vcat, map(components, x); init = Any[])
components(x) = Any[x]
width(::DistUInt{W}) where W = W

function warmup()
    a = flip(0.7)
    x = discrete(DistUInt{2}, [0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4])
    y = uniform(DistUInt{3}, 1, 6)
    z = ifelse(a, x + DistUInt{2}(1), x - DistUInt{2}(1))
    t = ifelse(flip(0.4), (a, z), (!a, x * x))
    e = prob_equals(z, DistUInt{2}(2)) | (x < z) | xor(a, flip(0.2))
    pr(flip(0.7))
    pr(a, z, y, t...; evidence = e)
    nothing
end

function dice_main()
    x1_ASIA = discrete(DistUInt{1}, [0.01, 0.99])
    x2_TUB = prob_equals(x1_ASIA, DistUInt{1}(0))
    if x2_TUB !== false
     x3_TUB = discrete(DistUInt{1}, [0.05, 0.95])
    end
    if x2_TUB !== true
     x4_TUB = discrete(DistUInt{1}, [0.01, 0.99])
    end
    x5_TUB = x2_TUB === true ? x3_TUB : x2_TUB === false ? x4_TUB : ifelse(x2_TUB, x3_TUB, x4_TUB)
    x6_SMOKE = discrete(DistUInt{1}, [0.5, 0.5])
    x7_LUNG = prob_equals(x6_SMOKE, DistUInt{1}(0))
    if x7_LUNG !== false
     x8_LUNG = discrete(DistUInt{1}, [0.1, 0.9])
    end
    if x7_LUNG !== true
     x9_LUNG = discrete(DistUInt{1}, [0.01, 0.99])
    end
    x10_LUNG = x7_LUNG === true ? x8_LUNG : x7_LUNG === false ? x9_LUNG : ifelse(x7_LUNG, x8_LUNG, x9_LUNG)
    x11_EITHER = prob_equals(x10_LUNG, DistUInt{1}(0))
    if x11_EITHER !== false
     x12_EITHER = prob_equals(x5_TUB, DistUInt{1}(0))
     x13_EITHER = x12_EITHER === true ? DistUInt{1}(0) : x12_EITHER === false ? DistUInt{1}(0) : ifelse(x12_EITHER, DistUInt{1}(0), DistUInt{1}(0))
    end
    if x11_EITHER !== true
     x14_EITHER = prob_equals(x5_TUB, DistUInt{1}(0))
     x15_EITHER = x14_EITHER === true ? DistUInt{1}(0) : x14_EITHER === false ? DistUInt{1}(1) : ifelse(x14_EITHER, DistUInt{1}(0), DistUInt{1}(1))
    end
    x16_EITHER = x11_EITHER === true ? x13_EITHER : x11_EITHER === false ? x15_EITHER : ifelse(x11_EITHER, x13_EITHER, x15_EITHER)
    x17_XRAY = prob_equals(x16_EITHER, DistUInt{1}(0))
    if x17_XRAY !== false
     x18_XRAY = discrete(DistUInt{1}, [0.98, 0.02])
    end
    if x17_XRAY !== true
     x19_XRAY = discrete(DistUInt{1}, [0.05, 0.95])
    end
    x20_XRAY = x17_XRAY === true ? x18_XRAY : x17_XRAY === false ? x19_XRAY : ifelse(x17_XRAY, x18_XRAY, x19_XRAY)
    x21_BRONC = prob_equals(x6_SMOKE, DistUInt{1}(0))
    if x21_BRONC !== false
     x22_BRONC = discrete(DistUInt{1}, [0.6, 0.4])
    end
    if x21_BRONC !== true
     x23_BRONC = discrete(DistUInt{1}, [0.3, 0.7])
    end
    x24_BRONC = x21_BRONC === true ? x22_BRONC : x21_BRONC === false ? x23_BRONC : ifelse(x21_BRONC, x22_BRONC, x23_BRONC)
    x25_DYSP = prob_equals(x24_BRONC, DistUInt{1}(0))
    if x25_DYSP !== false
     x26_DYSP = prob_equals(x16_EITHER, DistUInt{1}(0))
     if x26_DYSP !== false
      x27_DYSP = discrete(DistUInt{1}, [0.9, 0.1])
     end
     if x26_DYSP !== true
      x28_DYSP = discrete(DistUInt{1}, [0.8, 0.2])
     end
     x29_DYSP = x26_DYSP === true ? x27_DYSP : x26_DYSP === false ? x28_DYSP : ifelse(x26_DYSP, x27_DYSP, x28_DYSP)
    end
    if x25_DYSP !== true
     x30_DYSP = prob_equals(x16_EITHER, DistUInt{1}(0))
     if x30_DYSP !== false
      x31_DYSP = discrete(DistUInt{1}, [0.7, 0.3])
     end
     if x30_DYSP !== true
      x32_DYSP = discrete(DistUInt{1}, [0.1, 0.9])
     end
     x33_DYSP = x30_DYSP === true ? x31_DYSP : x30_DYSP === false ? x32_DYSP : ifelse(x30_DYSP, x31_DYSP, x32_DYSP)
    end
    x34_DYSP = x25_DYSP === true ? x29_DYSP : x25_DYSP === false ? x33_DYSP : ifelse(x25_DYSP, x29_DYSP, x33_DYSP)
    x35_result = (x20_XRAY, x34_DYSP)
    return x35_result
end

function report(k, x, d)
    if x isa AnyBool
        println("alea ", k, " true ", d[true])
        println("alea ", k, " false ", d[false])
    else
        for v in 0:(2^width(x) - 1)
            println("alea ", k, " ", v, " ", d[v])
        end
    end
end

function run_program()
    EV[] = true
    stats = @timed begin
        comps = components(dice_main())
        dists = pr(comps...; evidence = EV[])
        (comps, length(comps) == 1 ? [dists] : dists)
    end
    comps, dists = stats.value
    for k in eachindex(comps)
        report(k, comps[k], dists[k])
    end
    println("alea_seconds ", stats.time)
    println("alea_compile_seconds ", get(stats, :compile_time, NaN))
end

warmup()
task = Task(run_program, 1 << 30)
schedule(task)
wait(task)
end

#lang roulette/example/disrupt
;; racket bn.rkt NETWORK ASKS: a Bayesian network in Roulette's own BN
;; language, neuppl/roulette's `roulette/example/bn` (its reader and its
;; `make-run`, which the package's tests and the artifact's
;; benchmark/bayes.rkt run), on the BIF file NETWORK, asked what the file
;; ASKS asks, a line each:
;;
;;   order V ...   the variables evaluated, in this order (make-run's
;;                 var-order); every variable below and its parents are
;;                 among them
;;   observe V K   V observed at its K-th value (from 0, in the order the
;;                 file declares its values)
;;   query V       the distribution of V given the observations
;;   holds V K     with no query line: the probability that every holds
;;                 line's V takes its K-th value, nothing observed (P(e))
;;
;; The network is evaluated once at the module's level, the observations
;; observed there (`observe!`), and each query is asked as the language
;; asks an expression of a module (`display-pmf`: every random choice
;; summed out under the observations), its distribution read back from the
;; table it prints and printed in full, `roulette_b V VALUE P` for each
;; value of V of positive probability (VALUE as `write` writes it, as the
;; notes of Roulette's tddlog engine write the values of a call of
;; `infer`); with no query, `roulette_e P` for the holds lines'
;; conjunction. Reading the file is part of the run, as the artifact reads
;; its .bif inside its `time`.
(require racket/file
         racket/list
         racket/match
         racket/port
         racket/string
         (only-in roulette/example/bn make-run)
         (only-in (submod roulette/example/bn reader) [read bn-read])
         "print.rkt")

;; Every form of the module is a definition or a `statement` (print.rkt):
;; the language asks each expression of a module as a query of its own, two
;; calls of `infer` (its value's and its evidence's), and the circuit of
;; Roulette's tddlog engine numbers the calls, so that the K-th query here,
;; or P(e), is the (2K-1)-th call, as bench.py reads them.
(define ARGS (current-command-line-arguments))
(statement
 (unless (= (vector-length ARGS) 2)
   (raise-user-error 'bn.rkt "usage: racket bn.rkt NETWORK ASKS")))
(define NETWORK (vector-ref ARGS 0))

;; The blocks of the BIF file as `#lang roulette/example/bn`'s reader reads
;; them and `make-run` takes them: the reader's module is
;; (module _ LANG ... (define run (make-run 'BLOCKS)) ...).
(define BLOCKS
  (or (for/first ([f (in-list (call-with-input-file NETWORK bn-read))]
                  #:when (and (pair? f) (eq? (car f) 'define) (eq? (cadr f) 'run)))
        (cadr (cadr (caddr f))))
      (raise-user-error 'bn.rkt "~a: no blocks" NETWORK)))
;; Each variable's values, in the order the file declares them.
(define DOMAINS
  (for/fold ([h (hash)]) ([b (in-list BLOCKS)])
    (match b
      [`(variable ,v (type discrete (,_) ,vals)) (hash-set h v vals)]
      [_ h])))

(define (variable s)
  (define v (string->symbol s))
  (unless (hash-has-key? DOMAINS v)
    (raise-user-error 'bn.rkt "~a has no variable ~a" NETWORK v))
  v)
(define (value-of v k)
  (define vals (hash-ref DOMAINS v))
  (define i (string->number k))
  (unless (and (exact-nonnegative-integer? i) (< i (length vals)))
    (raise-user-error 'bn.rkt "~a has no value ~a of its ~a" v k (length vals)))
  (list-ref vals i))

;; The asks: the order, the observations and the holds lines as (variable
;; . value), and the queried variables.
(define-values (ORDER OBSERVED QUERIED HELD)
  (for/fold ([order #f] [observed '()] [queried '()] [held '()]
             #:result (values order (reverse observed) (reverse queried) (reverse held)))
            ([line (in-list (file->lines (vector-ref ARGS 1)))]
             #:unless (string=? (string-trim line) ""))
    (match (string-split line)
      [(cons "order" vs)
       (when order (raise-user-error 'bn.rkt "two order lines"))
       (values (map variable vs) observed queried held)]
      [(list "observe" v k) (values order (cons (cons (variable v) (value-of (variable v) k)) observed) queried held)]
      [(list "query" v) (values order observed (cons (variable v) queried) held)]
      [(list "holds" v k) (values order observed queried (cons (cons (variable v) (value-of (variable v) k)) held))]
      [_ (raise-user-error 'bn.rkt "not an ask: ~a" line)])))
(statement
 (unless ORDER
   (raise-user-error 'bn.rkt "no order line"))
 (unless (if (null? QUERIED) (null? OBSERVED) (null? HELD))
   (raise-user-error 'bn.rkt "holds lines ask P(e) alone: no observe or query line beside them")))

;; The network evaluated once: the value of each variable asked.
(define ASKED (remove-duplicates (append (map car OBSERVED) QUERIED (map car HELD))))
(define VALUE
  (for/hash ([v (in-list ASKED)]
             [x (in-list (call-with-values (λ () ((make-run BLOCKS) ASKED ORDER)) list))])
    (values v x)))

(statement
 (for ([o (in-list OBSERVED)])
   (observe! (equal? (hash-ref VALUE (car o)) (cdr o)))))

;; The distribution of x, a list of (value . probability): Roulette's query
;; at the module's level (`display-pmf`), read back from the table it
;; prints, or from the one value it prints alone (as dice2roulette.py's
;; programs read it).
(define (distribution x)
  (define text (with-output-to-string (λ () (display-pmf x))))
  (define (datum s)
    (define d (read (open-input-string s)))
    (if (and (pair? d) (eq? (car d) 'quote)) (cadr d) d))
  (define rows
    (for/list ([line (in-list (string-split text "\n"))]
               #:when (regexp-match? #rx"[│|]" line))
      (filter (λ (s) (not (string=? s ""))) (map string-trim (regexp-split #rx"[│|]" line)))))
  (if (null? rows)
      (list (cons (datum text) 1))
      (for/list ([r (in-list rows)]
                 #:unless (equal? r '("Value" "Probability")))
        (cons (datum (car r)) (string->number (cadr r))))))
(define (real p) (if (exact? p) (exact->inexact p) p))

(statement
 (for ([q (in-list QUERIED)])
   (for ([e (in-list (distribution (hash-ref VALUE q)))])
     (unless (member (car e) (hash-ref DOMAINS q))
       (raise-user-error 'bn.rkt "~a takes ~s, which it does not declare" q (car e)))
     (printf "roulette_b ~a ~s ~a\n" q (car e) (real (cdr e)))))

function report(k, x, d)
    if x isa AnyBool
        println("alea ", k, " true ", d[true])
        println("alea ", k, " false ", d[false])
